requirements.statement: With `Blocking: must-pass only` in `verification.md` and at least one criterion marked must-pass, a verification run whose open failures, once the inner fix loop and the closing regression pass are done, are all on criteria not marked must-pass ends `satisfied`; the result, state file and report list those failures, and each is written to the follow-up ledger (`discovered.jsonl`) as one product follow-up row (`rankClass: "product"`, `blocksFeature: false`).

With no blocking setting (section absent, line absent, or `verification.md` missing or unreadable), with `Blocking: all criteria`, or with no criterion marked must-pass (any TRD with none marked, and every sweep file), a failure on any criterion still prevents `satisfied`, exactly as today; and `/verify-build`'s fix rounds never build a failure the run listed as non-blocking.

A failure on a must-pass criterion prevents `satisfied` under either setting, including when the Judge's own exit wrongly says `satisfied`; the must-pass recheck (`applyMustPassRecheck`) and custody behave as today for must-pass criteria.
An invalid `Blocking:` value (anything but `all criteria` or `must-pass only`, or two `Blocking:` lines) is refused: verification is not run and the stop reason names the offending line.
The Judge never judges materiality and never applies the blocking policy: the policy is applied only by the workflow script, from the must-pass marks and the owner's setting.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives O5 (your instruction, 2026-11-12; PM decision 2026-11-11)

requirements.statement: The four-part definition from issue #113 (a main user flow broken; data lost or corrupted; private data exposed; money or AI spend charged wrongly) is stated in the TRD and success-definition authoring guidance as the test for which objectives to mark must-pass, with the note that verification-check rows (design comparison, data fidelity…) never carry a must-pass mark and so never block under `must-pass only`.
`/verification-setup` asks for the blocking policy, offering `all criteria` as the default, and writes it in a form the parser reads.

The shipped `verification.md` template carries the new short section with `Blocking: all criteria`, and a project still holding the current unfilled template is still recognised as unfilled after the template changes.

A headless fixture run (the `fixtures` environment in `verification.md`) with the policy set to `must-pass only`, one must-pass and one non-must-pass seeded defect, shows the non-must-pass failure listed as non-blocking, filed as a follow-up row, and the outcome `satisfied` only once the must-pass defect is met.
